policy_name: Leicestershire Police Artificial Intelligence Policy & Procedure
issuing_authority: Leicestershire Police (owner: Head of Corporate Services; approved by the Deputy Chief Constable)
regulatory_regime: Police force policy under UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018, MoPI and the Code of Ethics
geo_constraints: Leicestershire Police officers, staff, volunteers, contractors and anyone with access to the Force IT environment

locale_context.regulation: Internal force policy · mandatory, allow-list of approved tools with board approval of new AI
locale_context.culture: UK police-force operational policy: security-classification-driven and cautious, allowing only approved Microsoft Copilot tools and keeping AI out of evidential criminal-justice material, with human decision-makers retaining liability.

versions.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy & Procedure
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.

covered_entities: anyone given access to the Force IT environment
covered_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
covered_activities: use of AI tools in force work
use of AI outputs incl. in the criminal justice process
exceptions: AI MG form generation within the approved force trial with East Midlands CPS using GoodSAM AI
integrated AI tools within a wider adopted product do not need AI Board endorsement
conditions: OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE information (incl. personal data) may be used only with risk-assessed, explicitly authorised tools
new standalone AI tools require Artificial Intelligence Board approval
objective: Give clear direction on the responsible use of AI in Leicestershire Police so that all AI deployments are subject to robust oversight and risk management in line with legal, ethical and operational standards.

related_policies.policy: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018
UK Government Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI

conflict_rule: Use must comply with the Code of Ethics, data protection law and the Force's wider policies; the SIRO (Deputy Chief Constable) may revoke any AI use at any time.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/leicestershire_police.md). The asago copy is a Markdown conversion of the force document (tables as HTML, some list bullets lost, '100%' rendered as LaTeX). Annex A (governance process for new AI tools), referenced in §4.3, is not in the copy. Only the creation entry (21/10/2025) appears in the review log; the next review date is 01/05/2026, so a revised version may now exist (not checked). Numbering in §5.3 is duplicated in the original ('3.' and '6.' appear twice). Binding=false (not law); adherence is mandatory for all officers, staff, volunteers, contractors and others with access to the Force IT environment (§2).

clauses.original_text: As of the date of this document, the following represent the only standalone AI applications authorised for use by Leicestershire Police personnel: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (Free Version); Microsoft 365 Copilot (Licensed Version). No other standalone AI tools may be used within the Force.
clauses.requirement: only Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat / Copilot; consumer tools (ChatGPT, Deepseek, Gemini, Perplexity, self-hosted LLMs) prohibited
clauses.exception: new standalone tools approved by the Artificial Intelligence Board (§4.3)
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Bullet list flattened with semicolons (full stop added after the list). §5.3 item 2 adds: use a force account on a force device; personal accounts/devices prohibited.

clauses.original_text: However, due to the nature of policing and the critical importance of safeguarding sensitive operations, the following types of information must never be entered, pasted, uploaded, or otherwise submitted into Microsoft's Co-pilot or any other AI tool—regardless of the device or platform: Any data marked or implicitly classified as SECRET or TOP SECRET. … Covert Human Intelligence Sources (CHIS) Related Information …
clauses.object: SECRET/TOP SECRET data, CHIS information, information under handling conditions, legally privileged information, sensitive operational data, system credentials
clauses.requirement: never submit prohibited information types into any AI tool
clauses.exception: OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE (incl. personal data) permitted in risk-assessed, authorised tools
clauses.purpose: safeguard sensitive operations and national security
clauses.affected_asset: classified and operational police information; CHIS identities
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Other listed types elided with '…'. Guiding principle: if unsure, do not input it.

clauses.section: 5.3 What should I consider when using AI? – 4. Check the results
clauses.original_text: Check the results – AI is not 100% reliable and you must always read and verify anything produced.
clauses.affected_asset: accuracy of police records and decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: '100%' appears as LaTeX '$100\%$' in the Markdown copy (conversion artefact fixed).

clauses.section: 5.3 What should I consider when using AI? – 5. Be transparent
clauses.original_text: Be transparent – Don't claim AI produced work as your own. Although there is no need to declare every use of AI such as for note taking, drafting work you heavily edit or for research, transparency is essential to maintain the public trust so always declare the use of AI in any formal report, creative content or when it is used in decision making.
clauses.object: formal reports, creative content, AI-supported decisions
clauses.requirement: declare AI use in formal reports, creative content and decision-making
clauses.condition: formal reports, creative content or decision making
clauses.exception: note taking, heavily edited drafts and research need not be declared
clauses.affected_asset: public trust; integrity of police outputs
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Suggested note: 'Microsoft Copilot supported the creation of this document'.

clauses.section: 5.3 What should I consider when using AI? – 6. Human Review
clauses.original_text: Human Review - AI must not be allowed to make operational decisions without human review. AI can be used as a tool, to present options and wider considerations. However, the responsibility and liability remain with the police decision maker. AI can never be used as a defence or rationale for a poor decision.
clauses.requirement: no operational decisions by AI without human review; liability stays with the decision maker
clauses.affected_asset: rights of the public; police legitimacy
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)

clauses.section: 5.4 AI use in the Criminal Justice System
clauses.original_text: The use of AI technologies is not yet authorised for use in the Criminal Justice process, including for the creation of evidential materials. This means it must not be used in the preparation of witness statements, MG forms, or any other court ready evidential reports.
clauses.object: witness statements, MG forms, court-ready evidential reports
clauses.requirement: no AI in creating evidential material
clauses.exception: AI MG form generation in the approved force trial with East Midlands CPS using GoodSAM AI
clauses.purpose: integrity of evidence and fair trial
clauses.affected_asset: criminal justice process; defendants and witnesses
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI incl. integrated AI features and standalone generative AI tools (authorised: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: AI may support investigators in understanding evidence if it does not generate official evidential documentation.
